title: Bonds Behaving Badly - Systematic Investor 309

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Bonds Behaving Badly - Systematic Investor 309.docx

speakers: Katy Kaminski (chief research strategist, AlphaSimplex, guest co-host)
summary: Katy Kaminski and Niels Kaastrup-Larsen review the August 2024 yen carry unwind and trend-following performance. Main points: bonds misbehave (positive stock-bond correlation, higher vol) when inflation is higher, long-short trend diversifies a 60/40, and crisis alpha and carry are tested only by sustained shocks.

coverage.note: intro, sponsor disclaimer, small talk; BoJ hike and bond purchase cut as the catalyst
divergent vs convergent world; convergent portfolios; carry as convergence trade
convergence strategies fragile; August trend performance and model adaptability
signal speed, CTA decomposition, commodities, sector themes, trend barometer
index performance numbers, big S&P daily swings, regime view; set-up of the bond paper
bond paper: stock-bond correlation and volatility by inflation regime; inflation waves
inflation volatility, why not replace trend with bonds, carry, cash in short paper
2022 flight-to-safety failure, conditional bond distribution, bond vigilantes
alternatives to 60/40: long-short trend in bonds, dollar, gold, commodities; gold myth
gold timing, static 60/40, crisis alpha vs correction, July-August two-stage
trend pivot toward recession signals; first/second responders; vol spike; short-term strategies
crisis alpha is searched; non-trend sleeves; carry in CTAs and Covid
carry leverage risk, consistency tradeoff, VIX 65 calculation question
Aug 5 anatomy, VIX stress feedback, VIX calculation, price-only trend models
VaR crowding, 12% day, buffer fund rebalancing, not overreacting, AI
outro and ratings plea; nothing new

completeness_estimate: 0.90 - the first reader caught nearly every mechanism and number; misses were secondary points (inflation-volatility agreement incl. deflation, Japan crowding, investor inexperience, stress periods as tests, geopolitics).

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Bo J only increased by 15 basis points but then they mentioned this tiny reduction of quarterly uh purchases of uh of bonds
claims.claim: A small BoJ hike plus a tiny cut in bond purchases was enough to start a market unwind, showing how fragile unwinding of long-running monetary policy is.
claims.indicator: BoJ policy rate and quarterly JGB purchases

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: whenever you have more Divergence across Global economies you have more opportunities in some sense because there's just not one narrative they're multiple narratives
claims.claim: When central banks stop moving in sync, multiple macro narratives create tactical and dynamic opportunities, which favours active management after 2020.
claims.conditions: post-2020 regime of unsynchronised central banks
claims.testable: partly - divergence could be measured but the claim is regime-level

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: actually 85% or 90% of them are actually convergent strategies and there's a very small sliver of Divergent strategies
claims.claim: Typical endowment and pension portfolios are 85-90% convergent strategies that are implicitly short volatility, with very few divergent strategies.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: your classic convergence strategy is the carry trade
claims.claim: Carry is the classic convergence strategy and is vulnerable in shocks, so the August unwind exposed the weakness of convergent strategies.
claims.conditions: when the shock breaks the consensus soft-landing view
claims.testable: yes - carry returns in shock episodes

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: that's kind of what you're seeing in Trend signals as a result of this recent event
claims.claim: After the August shock trend signals started moving away from the convergent soft-landing view toward a recession-type positioning.
claims.testable: yes - trend signals can be read

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: convergence strategies are much more vulnerable in that scenario
claims.claim: Convergence strategies assume things return to normal and are hurt by unexpected shocks such as Covid, while divergent managers ask where the market could go next.
claims.testable: partly - depends on how strategies are classified

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: to me at least when I think about orca so far it's almost like the first half of the year in Reverse where we had a strong q1 and a weak Q2
claims.claim: Trend following in 2024 looked like the first half reversed (strong Q1, weak Q2, weak start of August, better last week), with July a precursor to August.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: some of the trend models uh would have picked up a while back a few weeks back maybe couple of months back that something was starting to look different
claims.claim: Some trend models flagged weeks to months before the BoJ move that the long equity, short yen theme was tiring, so trend can adapt before an event.
claims.indicator: trend signals on equities and yen
claims.testable: yes - signal histories can be checked

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: faster models um would have been less affected because there was some information leak in the price movements in the last few months
claims.claim: Faster trend models adjusted earlier ahead of the August shock because recent price moves leaked information, while long-term models were still anchored on early-year moves.
claims.conditions: when a reversal follows a long trend

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: longer term models which is pretty much the predominant um theme in our space it's because it has a higher sharp
claims.claim: Long-term trend (classic 12-month momentum) dominates in practice because it has a higher Sharpe ratio.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: earlier on a lot of ctas actually had a much faster models than they do today
claims.claim: A deconstruction of the SG Trend Index since 2000 shows CTAs used faster models earlier; in a less converging, more divergent world shorter signals may work better again.
claims.indicator: SG Trend Index decomposition by speed
claims.conditions: regime of divergent policy and fast moves (Covid-like)

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the bcom got decimated in the last three months or so
claims.claim: Commodities were tricky: a spring reflation rally (copper) reversed in summer and the Bloomberg Commodity index fell sharply, favouring shorter horizons there.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it's been you know it's been the equities that been struggling performance-wise
claims.claim: In the period trend losses came from equities and the yen, partly offset by grains and softs, with bonds in between depending on timing.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: my own Trend barometer finished at 39 yesterday
claims.claim: The host's Trend Barometer at 39 signals neutral to weak performance for trend followers.
claims.testable: yes - barometer is a defined series

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: btop 50 was down 2 and a qu% for the month
claims.claim: August performance: BTOP50 about -2.25% for the month and +2.99% YTD, SG CTA -3.12%, SG Trend -4.36%, short-term traders +0.62%, with MSCI World flat and S&P up 0.38%.
claims.indicator: BTOP50, SG CTA, SG Trend, SG Short-Term Traders

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we had the worst day for the S&P on Tuesday and the best day for the S&P in the last two years on Thursday
claims.claim: Within one week the S&P had its worst day and then its best day in two years, so a flat month hid large intramonth swings.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: until we figure out what's the new regime in a world where we no longer have you know correlated and coordinated Central Bank policy
claims.claim: Even with a low VIX, markets see undulations and fast sentiment shifts because central bank policy is no longer coordinated and the election and geopolitics are uncertain.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: stock Bond correlation goes positive when bonds experience inflation
claims.claim: When inflation is higher the stock-bond correlation turns positive, so bonds stop acting as the safety trade.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the average bond volatility is usually around 4% but during regimes and periods with higher um inflation Bond volatility goes up to maybe six on average
claims.claim: Average bond volatility is about 4% but rises to roughly 6% in high-inflation regimes, estimated over decades, which makes bonds a less stable base for 60/40.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: bonds would might even behave even worse uh in in in an unpredictable High inflationary uh period
claims.claim: Beyond the level of inflation, the volatility or unpredictability of inflation may make bonds behave even worse, though this was not tested.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: it doesn't tend to just disappear it tends to go in waves
claims.claim: Inflation tends to come in waves rather than vanish, so a smooth downward move in CPI does not mean bonds are safe again.
claims.conditions: after supply, geopolitical or other shocks
claims.testable: partly - wave pattern can be tested

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: because we had such a long time of stable low inflation uh on the backside of that you're also going to have a much more quote unquote violent reaction
claims.claim: After decades of stable low inflation and falling rates the reaction on the way back may be more violent, though the speaker has no way to know.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: trend has the ability to go both long and short fixed income
claims.claim: Trend portfolios (about 85% in fixed income) can go long or short bonds, unlike buy-and-hold, which remains exposed to valuation changes whatever yield is locked in.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: there's actually carry in derivatives portfolios right now which is non-negligible
claims.claim: With rates at about 5% the cash collateral and carry in futures portfolios are now a meaningful return source, which was missing for years.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: if you have a portfolio of bonds you're still susceptible to valuations over time
claims.claim: Locking in a 5% bond yield is not risk-free: entry timing and rolling at a changing curve create volatility, and yields fall fast when they fall.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: has you know 80% uh uh free cash and we put it into you know up to a Year's worth of of paper we know it's going to have a very beneficial effect
claims.claim: A trend fund holding spare cash in short-dated paper earns yield without taking the reaction-pattern risk an outright long-duration bond buyer takes.
claims.indicator: short-duration paper in managed futures cash

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: My Equity is going down but this portfolio of bonds that I have to collateralize it is also down
claims.claim: In 2022 bonds failed as a hedge and fell with equities, so mark-to-market valuation of bonds still matters even if the yield is locked in.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: you see a negative average distribution you also see a much wider range of values and you see a few very large fat-tailed left skew events
claims.claim: When equities fall, bond returns are good when inflation is low (right-shifted, thin left tail) but negative on average, wider and fat-tailed to the left when inflation is high.
claims.indicator: conditional bond return distribution in equity down periods by inflation regime
claims.direction: Bonds hedge only in low inflation

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: at some point with the level of deficits we see and how they continue to expand at some point I'm not predicting that
claims.claim: Growing deficits and bond vigilantes (as in the UK) could eventually reduce the safe-asset quality of government bonds.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: long short positions in fixed income so being able to be long or short had a negative correlation with equities during down periods
claims.claim: Long-short trend in bonds, the dollar and gold had negative correlation with equities in equity-down periods, and commodities went from strongly positive to flat, which diversifies a 60/40.
claims.indicator: long-short trend in bonds, dollar index, gold, commodities

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: if you just add long only bonds you have something that goes from negative to positive correlation that also increases inol
claims.claim: Portfolio diversification depends on correlation and added volatility: long-only bonds raise correlation and volatility, while vol-managed assets with negative down-period correlation diversify more.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I just don't see any consistency in that argument
claims.claim: The claim that being long gold always helps in equity downturns or inflation spikes is not consistent in the data.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the timing of those is never perfectly syned with those markets
claims.claim: Gold may help on average in recessions or inflation, but the timing is never in sync, so tactical long/short gold fits better than always long.
claims.testable: yes - compare static vs trend gold

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: with the 6040 you have no ability to do that
claims.claim: A static 60/40 cannot adapt to environments where moves are not all long, whereas a dynamic long/short strategy can, and long-run averages hide decade-long gaps.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: for me a crisis is a sustained period of losses in markets meaning months to a couple of weeks at least whereas a correction is when the markets go down and then come back to where they
claims.claim: Crisis alpha is gain during sustained market losses lasting weeks to months; a correction that reverses quickly is not a crisis and trend followers are too slow to benefit from it.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: a big part of July was challenging for Trend followers and and then of course the first week of uh August very challenging
claims.claim: Trend suffered in two stages, July and the first week of August, per the Hedge Nordic review.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: there's very little ability to be that quick to react and we're following sort of medium to long-term General themes of the market
claims.claim: Because trend trades medium- to long-term themes, crisis alpha is in short supply in very quick market shocks.
claims.direction: Trend loses in fast V-shaped shocks

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: they have long fixed income views and short commodity views and neutral and in the dollar that looks a lot more like a recessionary type signal
claims.claim: Trend signals moved from short bonds, long equities, long commodities and long dollar to long bonds, short commodities and neutral dollar, a recession-type profile.
claims.indicator: trend signals across bonds, commodities, dollar, equities
claims.conditions: if the correction turns into a crisis

correction.issue: Omits that trend signals, although weak, were still slightly long equities; the profile is not a full recession flip.
correction.fix: Trend signals moved from short bonds, long equities, long commodities and long dollar to weak signals that are still slightly long equities but long bonds, short commodities and neutral the dollar, which looks more like a recession-type profile.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the First Responders are things that actually benefit when the Vic spikes
claims.claim: First responders (short-term trading, options) profit when the VIX spikes but are hard to capture because they must be on the right side at the start.
claims.conditions: immediately at the start of a shock

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the second responders are things that kind of see that something is changing change positions with it and then eventually follow that that train
claims.claim: Second responders such as trend followers change positions after a shift is visible and ride a sustained crisis; the real value is in prolonged periods.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: volatility would have spiked and we will pick that up regardless of whether prices go back to where they came from
claims.claim: Even if prices revert, a vol spike changes volatility-targeted position sizes in trend programs, so a quick correction can still affect positions.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: a short-term strategy might do really well in the first or second day of a um of quote unquote the the yeah again correction or crisis
claims.claim: Short-term strategies can win on days one and two of a shock but are on the wrong side if markets rebound immediately, as in August 2024.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: this is not a guarantee it's not a put option and it's really more about a strategy that's adapting to different macro environments
claims.claim: Crisis alpha is something trend searches for, not a guaranteed hedge or put option; it appears only when the world moves in a drastically different direction.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we do 70% Trend or 80% Trend and then we have 20% or 30% non- Trend diversifying strategies
claims.claim: Many trend managers now run 70-80% trend plus 20-30% non-trend diversifiers, one of which is carry.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the carry Factor comes up more prominently in uh CTA returns over time
claims.claim: A study of CTA evolution found carry and other non-trend factors increasingly present in CTA returns, because managers added convergent strategies to smooth returns after trend struggled.
claims.indicator: carry factor loading in CTA returns

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: all started with kind of the carry trade being unwind
claims.claim: The early-August losses of a Nordic CTA seem linked to carry sleeves hit by the yen carry unwind, a rare test of carry within CTAs over the last 20 years.
claims.indicator: carry sleeve in CTA, yen carry trade

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: carrye being convergent being pure Trend and being faster was a better better equipped to deal with covid
claims.claim: In Covid, carry being convergent hurt while pure and faster trend was better equipped, because the event was violent and short.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: especially if you're doing it relative value with leverage
claims.claim: Carry exposure is most dangerous when run relative-value with leverage; directional carry with controlled leverage was less damaged.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: maintaining a big exposure to carry generally doesn't work as well during those environments
claims.claim: Carry is great until it isn't; a large carry allocation waters down a trend program's ability to capture crisis alpha, as seen in Covid.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: people love Trend in 2022 when everything is roaring but then they really don't like it in 20123 when it's giving back some of those profits
claims.claim: Investors want smooth returns but pure trend cannot give that; adding carry smooths lean times but creates losses in a crisis, a real tradeoff.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it's a very short uh window of time they use the uh for for the options that they that prices the vix
claims.claim: The VIX reading of about 65.7 on Aug 5 came from a very short window of option quotes, while the VIX futures were far lower, so the headline number may have overstated stress.
claims.conditions: at the open on illiquid quotes

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the bonds actually didn't rally on Monday that much so it was less of a riskof move
claims.claim: Monday Aug 5 was an equity shock from the carry unwind and yen move, not a classic risk-off, since bonds did not rally much, unlike the risk-off Friday.
claims.indicator: bond and yen moves around Aug 5

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: stress levels of individuals were directly correlated to the vix
claims.claim: MIT studies found traders' physiological stress correlated with the VIX, so a mis-measured VIX can feed back into panic.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: in the calculation of the vix apparently you you also look at just a bit offer spread and it's not real just traded prices
claims.claim: The VIX calculation uses bid-ask quotes rather than only traded prices, which may need to be revisited.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the only truth really is price and that's what we use in our models
claims.claim: Trend models use price only and size positions by each market's own volatility rather than VIX, unless trading the VIX itself.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: everybody if everybody follows VAR and we all have to deliv at the same time
claims.claim: If many investors use VaR risk models they must deleverage at the same time, amplifying selloffs, though not all trend followers use VaR.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: equities can actually drop 12% in the day
claims.claim: Equities can fall 12% in a day (Covid, Japan) out of nowhere; all it takes is a catalyst to shift sentiment.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: there's also a lot of people out there that are using sort of buffer funds and other things that also use options and if those go way out of range then there's rebalancing
claims.claim: Nervous investors plus a Japan catalyst led to deleveraging, magnified by risk limits and rule-based rebalancing of buffer funds, like 1987 portfolio insurance.
claims.conditions: when options go far out of range

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: oftentimes what we've learned is not overreacting is probably the best thing to do
claims.claim: Not overreacting is usually best: those who sold at Monday's low after seeing VIX 65 missed the rebound, and systematic managers should stick to the process.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: a big move like that is really hard to predict it's really hard to trade
claims.claim: AI would not have helped in the August shock; big moves are hard to predict or trade.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: with all the global conflict we have right now when people start shooting and firing rockets at each other it doesn't take much for something to go wrong
claims.claim: Beyond policy divergence, active geopolitical conflicts are a separate source of sudden shocks with large unintended market consequences, adding to a less stable regime.
claims.testable: partly - would need a geopolitical risk index vs. shock frequency

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: most invest out there have not seen inflation or if they did you know it's what their parents told them about it because they didn't perhaps invest during the 70s
claims.claim: Most investors have no first-hand experience of investing through inflation (the 1970s), so they are surprised and frustrated when bonds stop acting as the safety trade in inflationary periods.
claims.testable: no - investor experience is not directly measurable

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: volatility in inflation should also have a a naturally complex and create more volatility for fixed income and make things more complicated
claims.claim: Agreeing with the host, volatile inflation in either direction (including a slide into deflation or a renewed shock from geopolitics or supply chains) should itself raise fixed income volatility, separately from the inflation level.
claims.direction: higher inflation volatility -> higher bond volatility
claims.conditions: uncertain inflation path, supply-chain or geopolitical shocks
claims.testable: yes - regress bond volatility on rolling inflation volatility (not studied in the paper)

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: if that's what you're doing every day then you got to do that the other days and I think that's hard
claims.claim: Catching one-day extreme moves requires a strategy that trades that way every day, bearing its costs and losses on all the ordinary days, so such moves are very hard to capitalise on in practice.
claims.testable: partly - compare short-term strategy returns on shock days vs all other days

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: turned into Japan and sort of a systemic effect of Japan and how many people were in positions related to Japan on Monday
claims.claim: The August 5 2024 move escalated from an ordinary risk-off into a systemic event because so many investors held crowded Japan-related positions that had to be unwound at once.
claims.testable: partly - positioning data (CFTC yen shorts) before vs size of the move

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: investors can use for for assessing some of the uh the strategies they've been looking at or invested in um to see how they deal with these uh situation
claims.claim: Short stress episodes such as early August 2024 are useful out-of-sample tests for investors to assess how the strategies they hold or consider actually behave in a shock.
claims.testable: yes - event-study of manager returns over stress windows
